about.title: About
about.intro: LAST SIGNAL is a museum out of this world: fifteen machines NASA left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space, told with verified facts.
about.challengeText: A project for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: telling students and casual fans what the hardware left behind is, why it was sent and what it discovered.
about.code: How to tell fact from fiction
about.codeIntro: Each kind of content has its own style. Here is what each one looks like:

examples.machine: The machine's voice: imagined narration, in italics with big quotation marks.
examples.lumi: LUMI, the fictional guide: a cyan bubble with its avatar.
examples.log: Mission Log: verified facts with their source.
examples.photo: Real photo: with NASA title, date and credit.
examples.sonification: Sonification: data turned into sound; in space there is no air to carry sound.

about.teamText: We are a team taking part in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Everyone who contributed code is listed in the project repository. We don't publish personal contact details.
about.aiText: This site was built with the help of an AI assistant; the team checked the data against NASA sources.
about.aiDetails: Narration uses the browser's built-in speech synthesis ("Synthetic voice"). No AI-generated images, audio or data are used: sound is synthesized live and light times are calculated from JPL orbital elements.
about.creditsText: Open-source libraries (React, three.js, React Three Fiber, GSAP under its free standard license, Lenis, Zustand, i18next and more) and fonts under the SIL Open Font License: Unbounded, Fraunces, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and JetBrains Mono. Full list in CREDITS.md.
about.privacyText: No accounts, no cookies and no analytics. Your progress is saved only in this browser and you can erase it in Settings.
about.aiFile: Read the full disclosure (AI_DISCLOSURE.md, opens in a new tab)
about.repoNewTab: See the code and CREDITS.md (opens in a new tab)
about.contributors: See who contributed (opens in a new tab)
about.lumiWho: LUMI is a character made up for this website: a small listening probe that guides you. There is no real mission with that name.
about.nasaNote: We don't use NASA logos, insignia, flags or mission patches. The passport patches are original geometric designs.
